content: The NANS gene encodes the enzyme sialic acid synthase in humans. This enzyme plays a critical role in the biosynthetic pathways responsible for the production of sialic acids. In laboratory conditions, the protein produced by this gene utilizes N-acetylmannosamine 6-phosphate and mannose 6-phosphate as substrates. These substrates are converted into phosphorylated forms of N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac) and 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-glycero-D-galacto-nononic acid (KDN), respectively. However, the enzyme demonstrates significantly higher catalytic activity toward the production of Neu5Ac phosphate compared to KDN phosphate. When this gene is expressed in insect cells, it leads to the production of both Neu5Ac and KDN. The NANS gene shares a relationship with the sialic acid synthase gene neuB found in Escherichia coli (E. coli). Furthermore, the human NANS gene can partially compensate for the loss of sialic acid synthase activity in an E. coli mutant lacking the neuB gene.
